questions.enonce_markdown: Solve the equation $\cos x = \sin 2x$ in the interval $0 \le x \le \pi$. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the double angle formula $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$:

$$\cos x = 2\sin x\cos x \;\Longrightarrow\; \cos x - 2\sin x\cos x = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; \cos x\,(1 - 2\sin x) = 0.$$

(Do **not** divide by $\cos x$: that would lose the solution $\cos x = 0$.)

Either $\cos x = 0$ or $\sin x = \dfrac12$.

- $\cos x = 0$ in $[0, \pi]$: $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
- $\sin x = \dfrac12$ in $[0, \pi]$: $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ or $x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$.

$$\boxed{x = \frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{\pi}{2},\ \frac{5\pi}{6}}$$

Check: for $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\cos x = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\sin 2x = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$. For $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, both sides are $0$ ($\sin\pi = 0$). For $x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$, $\cos x = -\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\sin 2x = \sin\dfrac{5\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Express $5\cos x - 12\sin x$ in the form $R\cos(x + \alpha)$, where $R > 0$, and $0^\circ < \alpha < 90^\circ$, giving the value of $\alpha$ correct to one decimal place.

Hence or otherwise, find the minimum and maximum values of
$$\frac{10}{|5\cos x - 12\sin x| + 15}.$$
(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Harmonic form.** Expand $R\cos(x + \alpha) = R\cos\alpha\cos x - R\sin\alpha\sin x$. Matching with $5\cos x - 12\sin x$:

$$R\cos\alpha = 5, \qquad R\sin\alpha = 12.$$

Squaring and adding: $R^2 = 25 + 144 = 169$, so $R = 13$. Dividing: $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{12}{5}$, so $\alpha = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{12}{5} = 67.38^\circ$, which lies in $0^\circ < \alpha < 90^\circ$ (both $R\cos\alpha$ and $R\sin\alpha$ are positive).

$$\boxed{5\cos x - 12\sin x = 13\cos(x + 67.4^\circ)}$$

**Extreme values.** Since $-1 \le \cos(x + \alpha) \le 1$,

$$0 \le |5\cos x - 12\sin x| = 13\,|\cos(x+\alpha)| \le 13,$$

and both ends are attained ($0$ when $\cos(x+\alpha) = 0$, $13$ when $\cos(x+\alpha) = \pm1$). The denominator $D = |5\cos x - 12\sin x| + 15$ therefore satisfies $15 \le D \le 28$. The fraction $\dfrac{10}{D}$ is decreasing in $D$, so it is largest when $D$ is smallest and smallest when $D$ is largest.

- Maximum: $D = 15$, value $\dfrac{10}{15} = \dfrac{2}{3}$. It occurs when $5\cos x - 12\sin x = 0$, i.e. $\tan x = \dfrac{5}{12}$ ($x = 22.6^\circ$ plus multiples of $180^\circ$).
- Minimum: $D = 28$, value $\dfrac{10}{28} = \dfrac{5}{14}$. It occurs when $|5\cos x - 12\sin x| = 13$, i.e. $\cos(x + 67.4^\circ) = \pm 1$ ($x = 112.6^\circ$ plus multiples of $180^\circ$).

$$\boxed{\text{maximum} = \frac{2}{3}, \qquad \text{minimum} = \frac{5}{14}\approx 0.357}$$
